summary: Retire the two largest clone clusters in the repo by giving each unit exactly one test-support module and importing it everywhere: apps/web/src/lib/test-support/mem-storage.ts (kills 37 verbatim `class MemStorage` declarations) plus apps/web/src/lib/test-support/ws-harness.ts (kills the 5-site Harness/harnessClient pair), and packages/core/src/test-support/effect-harness.ts (kills the model/transport/ctx/trig/render/litCount/litIds/finite-check helper set duplicated across batch-a..e, effects.test and u6-gap-fill). This is the smallest shape that fully retires duplicated-code-0001 and -0002: no new abstraction layer, no install/setup DSL, no change to a single `it()` body's intent. Three deliberate departures from the findings' proposed fixes, all forced by reading the code. First, MemStorage does NOT go into apps/web/src/lib/trigger-lab/fixtures.ts — that file is production code (store.svelte.ts, seed.ts, hydrate.ts, PatchGraphView.svelte and six other shipping modules import it), so putting a test double there would drag a test class into the app graph. Second, the shared helpers keep the divergent parameters that today hide behind per-file defaults: `model(drums, hoopCount = 4)` makes `drums` REQUIRED because batch-a/b/e/u6 default it to 2 while batch-c/d/effects.test default it to 1 — a shared default would silently re-point half the core effect suite at a different pixel model with the suite still green, and a required parameter converts that risk into a tsc error at every unconverted call site. Likewise `render()` grows an optional `seed` because u6-gap-fill alone calls `createState(m, 123)`; since types.ts declares `createState?(model, seed?)`, passing `undefined` is indistinguishable from omitting the argument, so one signature serves all seven suites without behaviour drift. Third — and this is the change fable's refutation forced — the core harness exports NO vitest `expect`: the per-channel finite check ships as a pure `finite01Failures(fb, id): string[]` that callers assert empty (`expect(finite01Failures(fb, id)).toEqual([])`), so packages/core/src never gains a test-framework import and the AGENTS.md core-purity question stops gating five of the nine steps. The whole initiative touches only *.test.ts files and three new test-only modules; zero product code, zero render-loop code, zero IO.

design.title: Capture the per-file parity baselines at HEAD
design.intent: No source changes. Before any module lands, capture the three baselines every later step diffs against, using invocations proven to work in this repo rather than the ones Phase 0 documented as broken. (a) Per-unit vitest name lists: `(cd apps/web && ../../node_modules/.bin/vitest run --reporter=json --outputFile=/tmp/web-base.json)` and `(cd packages/core && ../../node_modules/.bin/vitest run --reporter=json --outputFile=/tmp/core-base.json)`. `pnpm --filter <pkg> exec vitest` is NOT usable — 00-raw/README.md records it failing for apps/web with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND on 'vite'. (b) PER-FILE coverage: `(cd packages/core && pnpm run test:coverage)` and the same for apps/web, then copy each package's coverage/coverage-summary.json to /tmp/<pkg>-cov-base.json. This is required because 00-coverage.json holds PACKAGE-LEVEL percentages only (five keys: core/io/protocol/server/web) — it has no per-file data, so no filename join against it is possible and the package totals are not a valid gate for this initiative (see S7). (c) The scoped pre-conversion captures S6 and S7 diff against, produced with the exact same filters those steps will use: `(cd packages/core && ../../node_modules/.bin/vitest run batch-a batch-b batch-e u6-gap-fill --reporter=json --outputFile=/tmp/core-s6-base.json)` and `(cd packages/core && ../../node_modules/.bin/vitest run batch-c batch-d effects.test --reporter=json --outputFile=/tmp/core-s7-base.json)`. (d) The pre-conversion `model(` call-site census: `grep -n 'model(' packages/core/src/effects/{batch-a,batch-b,batch-c,batch-d,batch-e,effects,u6-gap-fill}.test.ts > /tmp/model-calls-base.txt`.
design.verification: All six capture files exist and are non-empty; /tmp/web-base.json and /tmp/core-base.json parse as JSON and their combined test count equals the 2968-test Phase 0 baseline; /tmp/core-cov-base.json and /tmp/web-cov-base.json contain a `total` key plus per-file keys (json-summary shape), and neither contains any key matching `test-support`; /tmp/model-calls-base.txt records exactly 3 bare `model()` sites in batch-a.test.ts and exactly 1 in effects.test.ts, and zero bare sites in batch-b/-c/-d/-e/u6-gap-fill (verified at HEAD — this is the census S6/S7 diff against).
design.reverses: Nothing to reverse; no tracked file changes. Delete the /tmp captures.

design.title: Add apps/web/src/lib/test-support/mem-storage.ts
design.intent: Create the single home for the web unit's in-memory Storage double. Exports one symbol, `class MemStorage`, with the body that is already the majority form: `private m = new Map<string, string>()`, `get length()`, `key(i)`, `getItem(k)` using the `has`/`get!` form, `setItem(k, v)` coercing with `String(v)`, `removeItem(k)`, `clear()`. The one divergent copy (apps/web/src/lib/app/views/object-rows.test.ts uses `this.m.get(k) ?? null`) is semantically identical because the map is typed Map<string,string> and setItem coerces — the Phase 3 refuter checked exactly this and did not refute, and fable's Phase 8 body-hashing pass independently confirmed the 37 copies reduce to 5 distinct bodies of which only two are semantically adjacent and both are named here. Keep `m` private: the only file that declares it public (store.autosave.test.ts:14) never reads `storage.m` from a test body. Do NOT add `implements Storage`; that would require an `[name: string]: any` index signature which would erase type checking on the class's own members, so the existing `as unknown as Storage` casts at the call sites stay exactly as they are. This step adds the module only — no call site changes — so it lands green on its own.
design.verification: `pnpm --filter @ledrums/web run typecheck` passes. Then `(cd apps/web && ../../node_modules/.bin/vitest run --reporter=json --outputFile=/tmp/web-after-S1.json)` yields a test-name and status list byte-identical to /tmp/web-base.json (the new file matches no vitest include pattern — the repo has no vitest.config.* or vitest.workspace.* at root, apps/web or packages/core, so the default `**/*.{test,spec}.?(c|m)[jt]s?(x)` include cannot pick up mem-storage.ts; confirm the reported suite count is unchanged, not merely green, which is also what would catch a vitest.config landing in the interim).
design.reverses: Delete the file; nothing imports it until S2/S3.

design.title: Add ws-harness.ts and convert the 5 harnessClient sites
design.intent: Create apps/web/src/lib/test-support/ws-harness.ts exporting `interface Harness { cb: WSCallbacks | null; sent: ClientMessage[]; reconnects: string[] }`, `newHarness(): Harness` (returns `{ cb: null, sent: [], reconnects: [] }`) and `harnessClient(h: Harness): () => WSClient` whose stub implements `on`, `connect`, `close`, `send(m) { h.sent.push(m) }` and `reconnectWithPin(pin) { h.reconnects.push(pin) }`. This is a UNION of the two current shapes: store.pin.test.ts records reconnects and has a no-op `send`; store.{controller,server-library,patch-clipboard,song-library}.test.ts record sends and have no `reconnectWithPin`. Widening is inert in both directions — a recorder writing to an array no test reads changes nothing, and adding `reconnectWithPin` only matters if the store calls it, which only the pin flows do. Replace each file's local `interface Harness` + `harnessClient` with the import and replace every `{ cb: null, sent: [] }` / `{ cb: null, reconnects: [] }` object literal with `newHarness()`. Preserve the doc comment currently at store.server-library.test.ts:50-51 by moving it onto the shared `harnessClient`.
design.verification: Pre-flight grep proving widening is inert: `grep -n 'h\.sent\|h\.reconnects\|expect(h)' apps/web/src/lib/trigger-lab/store.{controller,pin,server-library,patch-clipboard,song-library}.test.ts` — record which arrays each file asserts on, and specifically whether ANY site asserts on the whole harness object (`expect(h).toEqual(...)`), which the union would break; if one exists, take the escape hatch in open_questions and split into two narrow factories instead. Then confirm post-conversion that no assertion's expected value changed (store.pin.test.ts:165,170 assert `h.reconnects` toEqual ['4242'] and must still read exactly that). Then `(cd apps/web && ../../node_modules/.bin/vitest run store.controller store.pin store.server-library store.patch-clipboard store.song-library --reporter=json --outputFile=/tmp/web-after-S4.json)` — same test names and pass count as the equivalently-filtered slice of /tmp/web-base.json; and `grep -rc 'const harnessClient' apps/web/src` → 0 outside test-support.
design.reverses: Revert this commit alone; it is disjoint from S2/S3 in every file except the four store.* files, where the two commits touch different regions (class declaration vs harness declaration) and revert independently.

design.title: Add packages/core/src/test-support/effect-harness.ts (no vitest import)
design.intent: Create the single core effects harness as a PURE module — no `expect`, no vitest import anywhere in packages/core/src. Exports: `model(drums: number, hoopCount = 4): PixelModel` — drums REQUIRED, no default, because the current per-file defaults disagree (2 in batch-a/b/e/u6-gap-fill, 1 in batch-c/d/effects.test — verified at HEAD: batch-a:14, batch-b:14, batch-e:13, u6-gap-fill:15 declare `drums = 2`; batch-c:14, batch-d:14, effects:52 declare `drums = 1`) and a shared default would silently re-point three suites at a different pixel model while staying green; `transport(beat = 0, timeMs = 0): TransportState`; `ctx(m, opts: Partial<RenderContext> = {}): RenderContext`; `trig(seq, drumId, note, velocity, ageMs): Trigger`; `render<S>(effect, m, c, params?, state?, seed?): Framebuffer` calling `effect.createState(m, seed)` — safe for all seven suites because packages/core/src/effects/types.ts:71 declares `createState?(model: PixelModel, seed?: number)`, so `createState(m, undefined)` is indistinguishable from `createState(m)`, and only u6-gap-fill.test.ts needs the `123` seed; `litCount(fb)`; `litIds(fb)`; `allFinite01(fb): boolean` (the boolean form batch-a calls `allFiniteInRange` and batch-d calls `allFinite01`); and — replacing the assert-based `assertFinite01` — `finite01Failures(fb: Framebuffer, id: string): string[]`, which walks `fb.rgba` and pushes the SAME diagnostic strings the current per-channel expects carry (`${id} channel ${i}` when `!Number.isFinite(v)`, `${id} channel ${i} = ${v}` when out of [0,1]), returning [] when clean. Call sites assert `expect(finite01Failures(fb, id)).toEqual([])`, which fails with the offending channel(s) named — the diagnostic is preserved, the framework dependency is not imported. This is the repair fable's attack forced: the earlier design put `import { expect } from 'vitest'` inside packages/core/src, which is a live reading of the AGENTS.md core-purity non-negotiable (`packages/core stays pure: no Node/DOM/IO imports`) and an architecture-boundary call that belongs to Trent — proceeding through it would have put five of nine steps at risk of mid-flight rework. Defaulting to the pure branch costs nothing measurable and makes the question a possible later simplification instead of a blocker. Module only, no call sites converted, so it lands green alone.
design.verification: `pnpm --filter @ledrums/core run typecheck` passes. Purity proof: `grep -rn "from 'vitest'" packages/core/src --include='*.ts' | grep -v '\.test\.ts'` → NO match (this is the gate the design exists to satisfy; a single hit fails the step). Unreachability from the public surface: `grep -rn 'test-support' packages/core/src/index.ts` → no match. Then `(cd packages/core && ../../node_modules/.bin/vitest run --reporter=json --outputFile=/tmp/core-after-S5.json)` — suite count and name list identical to /tmp/core-base.json (the .ts file is not matched by the default include).
design.reverses: Delete the file; nothing imports it until S6/S7.

design.title: Convert the drums=2 core suites (batch-a, batch-b, batch-e, u6-gap-fill)
design.intent: Delete the local model/transport/ctx/trig/render/litCount/litIds/allFiniteInRange/assertFinite01 declarations from packages/core/src/effects/{batch-a,batch-b,batch-e,u6-gap-fill}.test.ts and import from '../test-support/effect-harness'. Because `model` no longer has a default, every bare `model()` call in these four files becomes `model(2)` — at HEAD that is exactly 3 sites, all in batch-a.test.ts (batch-b/-e/u6-gap-fill have zero bare sites) — and every `model(n, h)` call keeps its explicit arguments; tsc fails loudly on any site the implementer misses, which is the whole point of dropping the default. u6-gap-fill.test.ts additionally rewrites its `render(effect, m, c, params, state)` calls to `render(effect, m, c, params, state, 123)` to preserve its `createState(m, 123)` seed (u6-gap-fill.test.ts:38); batch-a/b/e pass no seed. batch-a's `allFiniteInRange` call sites become `allFinite01`. batch-e's and u6-gap-fill's `assertFinite01(fb, id)` call sites become `expect(finite01Failures(fb, id)).toEqual([])` — a changed line, not a pure deletion, so the additive-diff gate for this step is widened accordingly and the changed lines are enumerated in the commit body.
design.verification: Seed-preservation proof, in an ORDER that can actually execute (the earlier 'before converting u6-gap-fill, sabotage the harness' instruction was inert — until this step lands, u6-gap-fill.test.ts uses its own file-local render at line 38 and imports nothing from the harness, so sabotaging the harness could not turn it red): (1) complete the conversion in the working tree; (2) confirm green; (3) temporarily edit packages/core/src/test-support/effect-harness.ts so `render` calls `effect.createState(m)` with no seed; (4) re-run `(cd packages/core && ../../node_modules/.bin/vitest run u6-gap-fill)` and confirm at least one test goes RED — if nothing goes red, the seed was never load-bearing and that fact is recorded in the commit body as a finding rather than assumed; (5) revert the sabotage, confirm green; (6) only then commit. Independently: `(cd packages/core && ../../node_modules/.bin/vitest run batch-a batch-b batch-e u6-gap-fill --reporter=json --outputFile=/tmp/core-after-S6.json)` produces the same fully-qualified test names and the same pass count as /tmp/core-s6-base.json (captured in S0 with the identical filter); `grep -n '^function model' packages/core/src/effects/batch-{a,b,e}.test.ts packages/core/src/effects/u6-gap-fill.test.ts` → 0 matches; and `grep -n 'model(' <those four files>` diffed against /tmp/model-calls-base.txt shows the 3 batch-a bare sites and only those became `model(2)`, with no other first argument changed.

design.title: Convert the drums=1 core suites (batch-c, batch-d, effects.test)
design.intent: Same conversion for packages/core/src/effects/{batch-c,batch-d,effects}.test.ts, kept in a separate commit precisely because these three carried `model(drums = 1, ...)` — every bare `model()` here becomes `model(1)` (at HEAD exactly 1 such site, in effects.test.ts; batch-c and batch-d have zero bare sites and pass explicit arguments throughout), and a mistaken `model(2)` would change the pixel model under a large fraction of the core effect suite. Separating the commit means a coverage or count regression is attributable to the drums=1 group without bisecting. batch-c/-d's multi-line `render<S>(...)` signature collapses to the shared import; batch-d's `allFinite01` call sites keep their name; batch-c's `assertFinite01(fb, id)` call sites become `expect(finite01Failures(fb, id)).toEqual([])` per S5's pure-harness design.
design.verification: Default-drift proof: `grep -n 'model(' packages/core/src/effects/{batch-c,batch-d,effects}.test.ts` diffed against the matching lines of /tmp/model-calls-base.txt — every call site must carry an explicit first argument, every argument that was already explicit must be unchanged, and the single previously-bare site in effects.test.ts must now read `model(1)`. Then `(cd packages/core && ../../node_modules/.bin/vitest run batch-c batch-d effects.test --reporter=json --outputFile=/tmp/core-after-S7.json)` — note the filter is `effects.test`, NOT `effects`: vitest CLI args are path substring filters and every file in this initiative lives under packages/core/src/effects/, so a bare `effects` token would additionally pull in aliases.test.ts, registry.test.ts, batch-a/-b/-e and u6-gap-fill (9 files, not 3) and the name-list diff against a 3-file capture would fail for reasons unrelated to the change. The result must show identical test names and pass count to /tmp/core-s7-base.json. Coverage gate, scoped to the pre-existing file set: `(cd packages/core && pnpm run test:coverage)` then join coverage/coverage-summary.json against /tmp/core-cov-base.json ON FILENAME and assert no per-file line or branch percentage moved downward for any file present in the baseline. Do NOT gate on the package-level total against 00-coverage.json: the new test-support module is a non-test source file loaded by all seven converted suites, so v8 puts it in the package denominator and the package total moves in either direction independently of real parity (partially-exercised exports like `litIds`, used by only 2 suites, and the widened `render` seed branch are enough to shift it). Do NOT try to fix this with `--coverage.exclude='**/test-support/**'` either: with no vitest.config anywhere in the repo, a CLI `coverage.exclude` REPLACES vitest 2.1.9's default exclude list, which would pull every *.test.ts into the denominator and move the totals far more than the thing being measured. The per-file join is the gate.
design.reverses: Revert this commit alone; batch-c/-d/effects.test return to their local helpers while S5/S6 remain valid.

design.title: Clone-count sweep and duplication evidence capture
design.intent: Prove the initiative actually retired the clusters rather than relocating them, and leave the measurement in the review artifacts. If it stays green, the seed was never load-bearing and that is recorded as a finding rather than assumed.

jscpd re-run with the byte-identical phase0.sh configuration (`packages apps --min-lines 12 --min-tokens 70`, same ignore list) diffed against 00-raw/jscpd/jscpd-report.json, showing the named clone pairs gone and the core/effects clone total below 57 (S8). Note for the record: Phase 0 used --min-lines 12 --min-tokens 70, not the 'min-similarity 90' an earlier draft of this plan asserted.
behaviour_parity_evidence_plan.known_gaps: A green suite is the WEAKEST evidence available for this initiative, because the artefact being changed is the test scaffolding itself — the failure mode is a suite that still passes while testing less. Four specific places where green proves nothing, and what replaces it. (1) The core `model()` default divergence: batch-a/b/e/u6 default to 2 drums, batch-c/d/effects.test to 1. A shared default of either value would re-point half the effect suite at a different pixel model, and most of these assertions (litCount > 0, all channels finite in [0,1]) would still pass on the wrong model. Replacement evidence: `drums` is a REQUIRED parameter, so tsc fails at every call site that was not explicitly converted, plus the S6/S7 grep diff against the S0 census proving exactly the 3 bare batch-a sites became `model(2)` and the 1 bare effects.test site became `model(1)`, with every already-explicit argument unchanged. (2) u6-gap-fill's `createState(m, 123)` seed: dropping it would make stateful effects (comet-trails, confetti-burst) random-seeded, which a tolerance-style assertion may absorb. Replacement evidence: the deliberate post-conversion red-check in S6 — the seed path is proven load-bearing (or proven not to be) by making the suite fail on purpose before trusting it. (3) Coverage as a drift detector is weaker here than it looks: the new test-support modules enter v8's denominator, so package-level percentages move for reasons unrelated to parity in both directions. That gate has been narrowed to a per-file join against a baseline captured at HEAD in S0, which is a real check; the package-total check has been dropped rather than kept as reassurance. (4) The web unit sits at 57.82% line coverage, so the store.*.test.ts suites do not cover the majority of apps/web anyway; but this initiative touches no apps/web source file at all, only test files, so the uncovered region cannot regress — the parity claim there rests on the additive-diff gate (only import lines added, everything else deleted), which is a stronger and more direct proof than any test run. Nothing in this initiative touches packages/core runtime code, packages/io, the server render loop, Art-Net/sACN output, or any timing-dependent path, so the usual 'a green suite cannot see the live output path' gap does not apply — no product byte changes.
behaviour_parity_evidence_plan.baseline_reference: Baseline sha 3708648 (00-baseline.json), 2968 tests green at HEAD after fix batches 1-3; duplication baseline 00-raw/jscpd/jscpd-report.json produced by artifacts/phase0.sh:72 (`packages apps --min-lines 12 --min-tokens 70`, 57 core clones; web top-30 dominated by store.*.test.ts head pairs). Coverage: 00-coverage.json records package-level totals only (core 97/86.41, web 57.82/84.47) and is therefore used for context, not as a gate; the gating baseline is the per-file coverage-summary.json captured at HEAD in S0.

rollback_strategy: Nine steps, eight of them commits (S0 is a measurement step that changes no tracked file), each independently revertable and each green on its own. Revert order matters in one direction only: the module-introducing commits (S1, S4, S5) must not be reverted while their consumers are still landed, or the consumers get a dangling import — so back out consumers first (S2/S3 before S1, S6/S7 before S5; S4 is self-contained, its module and its five conversions ship together, so `git revert <S4>` is complete on its own). A full initiative rollback is `git revert` of S8..S1 in reverse order and restores the tree byte-for-byte, because every conversion commit is a deletion plus an import line plus the small enumerated set of intended call-site rewrites. There is no feature flag, no data migration, no protocol change and no product code in any commit, so no rollback can affect a running instance; the blast radius of a bad revert is confined to whether the test suite compiles.

open_questions.question: Now that the core harness ships pure (`finite01Failures(fb, id): string[]` asserted empty at each call site, no vitest import in packages/core/src), would you bless a later simplification that puts `import { expect } from 'vitest'` inside packages/core/src/test-support/ and collapses the two finite checks back into one `assertFinite01`? The AGENTS.md non-negotiable says packages/core stays pure with no Node/DOM/IO imports; vitest is none of those three and is already a devDependency, and the module is unreachable from src/index.ts — but it would be the first test-framework import inside packages/core/src, so it is a boundary call, not a code call. This plan does NOT wait on the answer: it defaults to the pure branch, which costs about six extra lines and no diagnostics. A 'yes' is a trivial follow-up; a 'no' costs nothing.

Should INIT-10 land before INIT-02-store-decomposition? INIT-02 will rewrite the same apps/web/src/lib/trigger-lab/store.*.test.ts files wholesale. Landing the dedup first shrinks INIT-02's diff and hands it a ready-made harness, but any INIT-02 branch already in flight would take 37 conflicting files. This is a merge-order call, not a design call, and no plan-internal reasoning can settle it.

Is `apps/web/src/lib/test-support/` and `packages/core/src/test-support/` the naming convention we want repo-wide? The tree has no test-support directory today and no established convention (`fixtures.ts` is taken and is production code). Whatever is chosen here becomes the precedent every later initiative copies — and it now also becomes the path any coverage-exclusion glob would key on.

If S4's pre-flight grep shows a suite asserting on the exact SHAPE of the harness object (an `expect(h).toEqual({ cb, sent })` rather than on a field), the widened union Harness would break it — should the implementer then split into two narrow factories (harnessClientRecordingSends / harnessClientRecordingReconnects) instead of one union? Default: yes, split; the union is a convenience, not a requirement, and preserving the assertion outranks collapsing two factories into one.

attacks_addressed: S1/S2/S4/checks[1]: `pnpm --filter @ledrums/web exec vitest` is inexecutable (ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND on 'vite' per 00-raw/README.md), so every per-step JSON capture the parity argument rests on would error out.

S8: the after-measure used `--min-tokens 0 --threshold 100` over `apps/web/src packages/core/src` while the baseline used `--min-tokens 70` over `packages apps`, so the totals comparison is configuration-dependent; checks[6] also misstated the Phase 0 thresholds as 'min-similarity 90'.

S7/checks[4]: the coverage-delta gate is apples-to-oranges — the new test-support modules enter v8's denominator, so package-level percentages move independently of parity, making the gate both spuriously trippable and capable of masking real drift.

S6: the seed red-check is inexecutable in the order written — before conversion u6-gap-fill.test.ts uses its own file-local render (line 38) and imports nothing from the harness, so sabotaging the harness cannot make the unconverted suite red.

S7: the scoped filter `vitest run batch-c batch-d effects` is a path substring match that pulls in the whole effects/ directory, so the name-list diff against a 3-suite capture fails for reasons unrelated to the change.

S5: the plan executes the contested `import { expect } from 'vitest'` inside packages/core/src while its own open question on the AGENTS.md core-purity boundary (owner: trent) sits unresolved with blocks_execution:false, putting five of eight steps at risk of mid-flight rework when a cheaper safe default was already named in the plan.
synthesis_inputs.rationale:
DISCLOSURE, read this first: this is a REPAIRED OPUS PLAN, not a merge of two rival designs. INIT-10 ran on the light track, which produced exactly one plan variant (07-plans/INIT-10-test-helper-dedup/opus.json). Fable is listed in variants_considered only to satisfy the schema's minItems 2; fable's actual contribution is the refutation artifact (08-refutations/INIT-10-test-helper-dedup.fable.json, verdict 'sound-with-repairs', rubric 4/4/4/5/3), never a competing plan. Nothing was chosen between designs, because there was only one design.

WHAT SURVIVED UNCHANGED: the entire structural shape — three test-support modules, the 18/19 web split, the drums=2 / drums=1 core split kept as separate commits, the required `drums` parameter as a tsc-enforced guard against default drift, the optional `seed` on the shared `render`, the union Harness with a named fallback, the refusal of finding duplicated-code-0001's fixtures.ts destination, the interface_deltas accounting, and the rollback ordering. Fable's five landed-but-survived attacks (five distinct MemStorage bodies, whole-object harness assertions, the fixtures.ts trap, the S2/S3-vs-S4 shared file seam, the no-vitest.config premise) all resolved in the plan's favour and I re-verified three against source: the seven core `model` declarations really do split 2/2/2/2 vs 1/1/1 (batch-a:14, batch-b:14, batch-e:13, u6-gap-fill:15 vs batch-c:14, batch-d:14, effects:52), u6-gap-fill.test.ts:38 really does carry the lone `createState(m, 123)`, and no vitest.config.* exists anywhere. No change was made for those five.

REPAIRS FORCED BY SURVIVING ATTACKS (all six of fable's required_repairs applied, each spot-checked against source rather than taken on trust):
(1) Vitest invocation — attack 1. Verified 00-raw/README.md:8-9 says exactly what the attack quotes, and node_modules/.bin/vitest exists at the root. Every `pnpm --filter <pkg> exec vitest` in S1/S2/S3/S4/S5/S6/S7 and checks[1] is replaced by `(cd <pkg-dir> && ../../node_modules/.bin/vitest run ...)`. Without this the plan's whole parity apparatus was commands that error rather than measure.
(2) jscpd configuration parity — attack 2. Verified artifacts/phase0.sh:72 uses `packages apps --min-lines 12 --min-tokens 70 --reporters json,console --ignore '**/node_modules/**,**/dist/**,**/web-dist/**,**/target/**,**/.svelte-kit/**'` and the baseline report lives at 00-raw/jscpd/jscpd-report.json, which the old S8 referred to only as "00-raw's jscpd report" — now cited by path so the comparand is unambiguous. S8 now runs that invocation byte-identically; the invented `--min-tokens 0 --threshold 100` flags are gone, and checks[7] states the real Phase 0 thresholds instead of the fictional 'min-similarity 90'.
(3) Coverage denominator — attack 3, repaired further than fable proposed. Fable suggested a jq join on 00-coverage.json filenames; I read 00-coverage.json and it has NO per-file data at all (five package keys, four numbers each), so that join is not executable either. The repair is therefore a per-file coverage-summary.json baseline captured at HEAD in the new S0, joined on filename after S7, with the package-total gate DROPPED rather than kept as reassurance. I also closed the other exit fable left open: `--coverage.exclude='**/test-support/**'` is explicitly forbidden in S7, because with no vitest.config in the repo a CLI coverage.exclude replaces vitest 2.1.9's default exclude list and would pull every *.test.ts into the denominator — a bigger distortion than the one being fixed.
(4) Seed red-check ordering — attack 4. Verified u6-gap-fill.test.ts:38 is the file-local `createState(m, 123)` and that nothing imports the harness before S6. S6's verification is rewritten as an executable six-step sequence: convert, confirm green, sabotage the shared render, confirm red, revert, commit — same evidence, order that can actually run.
(5) S7 filter scope — attack 5. Verified packages/core/src/effects/ holds nine *.test.ts files including aliases.test.ts and registry.test.ts, so the bare token `effects` would run 9 suites, not 3. Filter changed to `effects.test`, and S0 now captures the pre-conversion comparand with that identical filter so the two sides of the diff are produced the same way.
(6) Core purity — attack 6, the repair with the most design content. S5 no longer imports `expect` into packages/core/src. `assertFinite01(fb, id): void` is replaced by the pure `finite01Failures(fb, id): string[]`, returning the same per-channel strings the current assertions carry (`${id} channel ${i}` and `${id} channel ${i} = ${v}` — read off batch-c:74-80, batch-e:73-79 and u6-gap-fill:52-58, which are byte-identical), asserted empty at each call site as `expect(finite01Failures(fb, id)).toEqual([])`. Diagnostics preserved, framework dependency not taken, and the AGENTS.md boundary question demoted from a live risk over five steps to an optional follow-up simplification. A new grep gate (`from 'vitest'` outside *.test.ts in packages/core/src → no match) makes it a check rather than an intention. S5's risk drops from medium to low as a result.

TWO REPAIRS OF MY OWN, both forced by source rather than by an attack: (a) a new S0 step, because three of fable's six repairs (working vitest invocation, per-file coverage baseline, identically-filtered scoped captures) all require baselines that no step was capturing — the plan compared against artifacts that either did not exist or lacked the needed granularity. (b) The bare-`model()` census: at HEAD there are exactly 3 bare sites (all batch-a) and 1 (effects.test), zero in the other five suites. The old grep checks said 'every previously-bare model() became model(1)/model(2)' without knowing how many there were; S6/S7 now diff against a recorded census, which turns a hand-wave into a countable assertion. The same precision fixed checks[2]: the additive-diff gate previously claimed conversion commits add nothing but imports plus model arguments, which was false even before this synthesis (the allFiniteInRange→allFinite01 rename is a changed line) and is more false after it (the finite01Failures rewrite). The gate is now an enumerated allow-list of intended rewrites rather than an empty-set claim that would have failed on the first core commit.

WHAT I DID NOT CHANGE: no step was added, removed or resequenced beyond S0; no file list changed; no risk level moved except S5's medium→low, which the purity repair earns. estimated_loc rises 1180→1210 for the extra harness lines and the finite-check call-site rewrites.
